nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A clause on $n$ variables is a finite set $C$ of literals $(i, b)$, where $i \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ is a variable and $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$. An assignment $x : \{0, \dots, n - 1\} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies $C$ if $x_i = b$ for some literal $(i, b) \in C$.
nodes.title: Satisfied clause

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 2$, the number of unate $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables divided by the number of $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$; that is, the Bollobás–Brightwell–Leader conjecture holds for every $k$.
nodes.title: Nearly all $k$-SAT functions are unate

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every natural number $k \ge 2$, the number of unate $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables divided by the number of $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Bollobás–Brightwell–Leader conjecture for all $k$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, the proposition that if $k \ge 2$, then the number of unate $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables divided by the number of $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$; that is, a $1 - o(1)$ fraction of the $k$-SAT functions on $n$ variables is unate.
nodes.title: Bollobás–Brightwell–Leader conjecture for $k$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the number of Boolean functions $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ that are $k$-SAT functions on $n$ variables.
nodes.title: Number of $k$-SAT functions

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the number of Boolean functions $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ that are $k$-SAT functions on $n$ variables and are unate.
nodes.title: Number of unate $k$-SAT functions

nodes.summary: Let $k, n \in \mathbb{N}$. A Boolean function $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ is a $k$-SAT function on $n$ variables if there is a finite set $S$ of clauses on $n$ variables such that each clause in $S$ has at most $k$ literals, no two of them on the same variable, and for every assignment $x$, $f(x) = \mathrm{true}$ if and only if $x$ satisfies every clause in $S$.
nodes.title: $k$-SAT function

nodes.summary: Let $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ be a Boolean function and $i$ one of its $n$ variables. Then $f$ is negatively unate in $i$ if for all assignments $x$ and $y$ that agree at every variable other than $i$ and have $x_i = \mathrm{false}$ and $y_i = \mathrm{true}$, $f(y) = \mathrm{true}$ implies $f(x) = \mathrm{true}$. Equivalently, switching $i$ from false to true…
nodes.title: Negatively unate variable

nodes.summary: Let $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ be a Boolean function and $i$ one of its $n$ variables. Then $f$ is positively unate in $i$ if for all assignments $x$ and $y$ that agree at every variable other than $i$ and have $x_i = \mathrm{false}$ and $y_i = \mathrm{true}$, $f(x) = \mathrm{true}$ implies $f(y) = \mathrm{true}$. Equivalently, switching $i$ from false to true…
nodes.title: Positively unate variable

nodes.summary: A Boolean function $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ is unate if, for every variable $i$, $f$ is positively unate in $i$ or negatively unate in $i$.
nodes.title: Unate Boolean function

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
